outcome: Since 26 January 2024 a polynomial map C^3 to C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant -2 and no polynomial inverse has been announced (Levent Alpöge, 19 July 2026, credited to Claude Fable 5), checked algebraically by Terence Tao and in Isabelle/HOL, and extended to every dimension n >= 3 by padding and by follow-up families; the plane case n = 2 remains open in every source read, and no 2026 result had passed peer review in the latest sources read.
problem_asks: Read from the statement alone: (1) for any characteristic-0 field k; (2) for any n >= 1 and any polynomial map F = (F_1,...,F_n) with components F_i in k[x_1,...,x_n]; (3) hypothesis: the Jacobian determinant det(dF_i/dx_j) is a nonzero constant; (4) conclusion: F has a regular inverse, i.e. a map G with polynomial components such that F(G(y)) = y and G(F(x)) = x. The statement is a single universal claim quantified over every dimension n and every characteristic-0 field k. It does not single out n = 1 or n = 2, and it does not restrict the field beyond characteristic 0.

events.what_happened: Levent Alpöge announced on X an explicit polynomial map F: C^3 to C^3, F(x,y,z) = ((1+xy)^3 z + y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy), y + 3x(1+xy)^2 z + 3xy^2(4+3xy), 2x - 3x^2 y - x^3 z), with Jacobian determinant -2 and F(0,0,-1/4) = F(1,-3/2,13/2) = F(-1,3/2,13/2) = (-1/4,0,0), so F is not injective and has no polynomial inverse. The announcement is dated 19 July 2026 in Wikipedia's lead, in the Gao abstract, in Gallagher's preprint and in the Breakthrough Tracker record, and 20 July in Wikipedia's citation of the tweet, in the AFP entry and in Gallagher's reference list (see disputes). The map as written is reproduced in the minimaxir.com post, which quotes it from the announcement; it has degree seven and the same collision points as Tao's digest, which I checked by hand. The announcement itself was not reachable (X returned HTTP 402), so the wording here comes from secondary reports. No arXiv or journal version of this announcement was found.
events.delivers: Over C, and also over Q since the map has integer coefficients and rational collision points, shows the statement fails for n = 3: an explicit map with constant nonzero Jacobian determinant (-2) that is not injective, so has no polynomial inverse. Restriction: the announced map lives in dimension 3. The AFP entry (2026-07-20) and van den Essen's abstract state that identity padding gives counterexamples in every n >= 3, keeping the determinant constant; that extension is recorded under those events.
events.remains: For the statement as worded (all n, all characteristic-0 k): nothing is settled about n = 1 (trivial) or n = 2 (the plane case). Every source read, including Wikipedia's lead, Meng and Yang, Nguyen and MathWorld (updated 2 October 2026), says the plane case remains open. Whether the plane case is part of what the universal claim asks is a reading of problem_asks, not something this event decides.

events.directly_checkable: The explicit map above. For this record I checked by hand that the three points each map to (-1/4,0,0) and that the Jacobian determinant at the origin is -2. I did not check that the determinant is constant on all of C^3: a Python/sympy check was blocked by a permission prompt. Constancy rests on Tao's digest and the Isabelle entry.
events.direction: Against the conjecture in dimension 3: the map is exactly a constant-Jacobian polynomial map with no polynomial inverse, the kind of object the universal claim rules out. It does not bear on n = 2.
events.object: An explicit polynomial map F: C^3 to C^3 (also with integer coefficients), F(x,y,z) = ((1+xy)^3 z + y^2(1+xy)(4+3xy), y + 3x(1+xy)^2 z + 3xy^2(4+3xy), 2x - 3x^2 y - x^3 z), of degree 7. Its Jacobian determinant is the constant -2, and the three distinct points (0,0,-1/4), (1,-3/2,13/2), (-1,3/2,13/2) all map to (-1/4,0,0). The map is explicit, not a non-constructive existence proof.

events.what_happened: Alexis Gallagher (Repertory Robotics, Inc.) posted a Zenodo preprint, 'An infinite family of counterexamples to the Jacobian Conjecture in dimension three: every generic fiber degree n>=3 occurs' (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.21479195), building on Alpöge's three-variable counterexample. The record describes a uniform construction giving, for each integer n >= 3, an explicit polynomial map on C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant 1 and generic fibre degree exactly n, and says the degree-four member is not equivalent to Alpöge's degree-three map under polynomial coordinate changes and is not an iterate of it. The record says the identities were checked by exact symbolic or rational arithmetic and names no formal proof assistant. The PDF could not be extracted, so the formulas were not read.
events.revisions: Zenodo record: v1, created and modified 21 July 2026 (per the record page). No later version seen.
events.delivers: For each n >= 3, a further counterexample in dimension 3 (generic fibre degree n) with determinant 1, distinct from Alpöge's map. Restriction: dimension 3 as stated; higher dimensions not claimed in this record.
events.remains: n = 2 (the plane case) and, for the universal claim, nothing beyond the dimension-3 failure already in alpoge-2026-07-19. The family shows that the dimension-3 failure is not isolated.
events.directly_checkable: The family is said to be explicit (record page). The formulas were in the PDF, which I could not extract, so not checked.
events.direction: Against the conjecture in dimension 3, in the same sense as alpoge-2026-07-19, with one counterexample per generic fibre degree n >= 3.
events.object: An explicit family F_n: C^3 to C^3 (per the record: 'a uniform construction ... yields an explicit polynomial map on C^3 with constant Jacobian determinant 1 and generic fiber degree exactly n'). The explicit formulas were not read.

events.what_happened: Terence Tao, 'A digestion of the Jacobian conjecture counterexample', blog post dated 21 July 2026. An exposition of Alpöge's map: Theorem 2 states there is a polynomial F: C^3 to C^3 with non-zero constant Jacobian that is not invertible; equation (1) is the degree-seven map; det DF = -2 and the three collisions are stated; the post gives a geometric re-derivation in local-injectivity terms and says the map is hard to find by brute force. The post contains two AI statements, both quoted via a fetch summary: 'It was recently shown (using the Fable AI) that the conjecture is false in three dimensions' and 'AI disclosure: I used an AI chatbot to discuss various aspects of this problem and to confirm several of the calculations made here.' The second links to a ChatGPT share page. No new object beyond alpoge-2026-07-19.
events.delivers: Re-establishes in C^3, with an explanation, the non-invertibility of the map of alpoge-2026-07-19 with constant Jacobian -2. No new restriction beyond dimension 3.
events.remains: As for alpoge-2026-07-19: n = 2 open.

checked_by.what_they_did: Worked through the algebra, states the determinant and collisions, and says the map can be verified by a brief coordinate computation; discloses an AI chatbot used to confirm several calculations

events.what_happened: Archive of Formal Proofs entry 'Formal Verification of an Explicit Counterexample to the Jacobian Conjecture' by Arthur Freitas Ramos, David Barros Hulak and Ruy Jose Guerra Barretto de Queiroz, dated 20 July 2026. An Isabelle/HOL verification that Alpöge's explicit map has Jacobian determinant identically -2 and that three distinct rational points share an image, so the map has no polynomial inverse; it builds identity-padded maps giving counterexamples in every finite dimension >= 3, and makes no claim about dimension two. The entry says AI assistance was used for proof engineering (system not named in the text read) and that the announcement credits Claude Fable with work leading to the map (the entry's account of the announcement).
events.delivers: Machine-checked confirmation of alpoge-2026-07-19 for n = 3, and padded counterexamples for each n >= 3 (constant determinant preserved). No claim about n = 2.
events.remains: n = 2, as the entry states.

The full text was not read.

events.what_happened: Tanush Shaska, 'Graded Keller maps and the Jacobian Conjecture', arXiv:2607.20210 (v1 22 July 2026; v2 25 July 2026). Per the abstract: equivariant Keller maps for a weight grading; with all-positive weights an equivariant Keller map is always an automorphism, and in dimension two this holds for every sign pattern; over Q the image of the counterexample is a thin set; the abstract refers to 'the map recently announced as a counterexample', equivariant for the grading (1,-1,-2).
events.delivers: Partial structural results for equivariant (graded) Keller maps, restricted to graded maps. It does not settle the statement; the 2026 counterexample has negative weights, so the all-positive-weights theorem does not apply to it.

events.direction: Neutral to the statement; restricted to graded maps.

events.what_happened: Guowu Meng and Liang Yang, 'A five-variable counterexample to the Hessian conjecture, and the low-dimensional status of the Jacobian and Hessian conjectures', arXiv:2607.22198 (v1 24 July 2026; v2 27 July 2026). Per the abstract: an integer polynomial in five variables with constant Hessian determinant 128 and non-injective gradient, refuting the five-variable Hessian conjecture, built from a six-variable doubling of Alpöge's Jacobian counterexample. The paper states that the three-variable Jacobian conjecture is false (Alpöge), that JC_2 and HC_4 remain unsettled, and that HC_4 implies JC_2. It also updates the first author's earlier preprint.
events.delivers: For the Jacobian statement: a restatement that JC_3 is false and JC_2 is open. Its new counterexample is to the Hessian conjecture in dimension five, a different question.
events.remains: JC_2 (the plane case), per the paper.
events.directly_checkable: The five-variable polynomial (explicit, per abstract). Not read in full.

events.object: An integer polynomial in five variables, degree 14, with constant Hessian determinant 128 and non-injective gradient (a Hessian object, not a Jacobian one).

events.what_happened: Christopher D. Long, 'An Explicit Counterexample to the Rank-Two Poisson Conjecture', arXiv:2608.23777 (v1 22 July 2026, the only version; 17 pages, 1 table). Explicit rational polynomials R, T, D, S in four variables define a Poisson endomorphism of the rank-two canonical Poisson algebra that is not an automorphism; the paper says this disproves the Poisson conjecture for two canonical pairs and so for any number of pairs at least two. An appendix builds a non-automorphic endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra, which MathWorld reports as a proposed counterexample to the Dixmier conjecture for n = 4. MathWorld (updated 2 October 2026) says 'ChatGPT supplied the construction with additional AI auditing' and that independent verification had not been reported as of 7 September 2026. The arXiv abstract and comments contain no AI statement.
events.delivers: A counterexample to the Poisson conjecture for two or more canonical pairs (a different question), and, if the appendix holds, to the Dixmier conjecture for n = 4 (also a different question). The Dixmier conjecture is reported to imply the Jacobian conjecture (a HandWiki search snippet, not opened), so a Dixmier counterexample would not by itself settle the Jacobian statement either way.
events.remains: The Jacobian statement is not touched by this event.
events.directly_checkable: The rational polynomials R, T, D, S. Not checked by me.
events.direction: Against the Poisson conjecture (and, if the appendix holds, the Dixmier conjecture for n = 4). Neither bears on the Jacobian statement directly.
events.object: Explicit rational polynomial endomorphism R = x(2 - 3xq), with T, D, S, of the rank-two Poisson algebra, not an automorphism. The induced map of A^4 preserves the symplectic form, has Jacobian determinant one, and has a fibre of exactly three points (per abstract). Appendix: a non-automorphic endomorphism of the fourth Weyl algebra (per abstract).

events.what_happened: Thomas Prellberg, 'Collision-Generated Compression for Homogeneous Keller Maps', arXiv:2608.12543 (v1 12 Aug 2026; v2 31 Aug 2026; v3 15 Sep 2026). Defines the 'collision hull' of a collision in a homogeneous Keller map and applies it to two cubic-homogeneous reductions of the three-variable counterexample (Thompson's 24-variable map, and the 19-variable homogenisation of Van Rijn's map). Also gives a 340-monomial homogeneous quartic that is Hessian-nilpotent, violates Zhao's Vanishing Conjecture, and has an exact collision over Q(i). The page makes no AI statement and mentions a companion script for the finite checks.
events.delivers: Structural results on collisions in reductions of the dimension-3 counterexample. Not a new counterexample to the statement in dimension 3 (already in alpoge-2026-07-19). The quartic bears on the Hessian and Zhao conjectures (different questions).
events.remains: The statement in full, including n = 2.
events.directly_checkable: The collisions in the reductions and the quartic, with a companion script listed on the page (not read).
events.direction: Concerns reductions of the existing counterexample; does not change the truth value beyond alpoge-2026-07-19.
events.object: A 340-monomial homogeneous quartic that is Hessian-nilpotent, with an exact collision over Q(i) (per abstract; not read in full).

events.what_happened: Xiaoyang Chen and Xiang Jiang, 'Moonshine: An Autonomous Mathematical Research Agent Centered on Conjecture Generation', arXiv:2606.10806 (v1, 9 June 2026, the only version). Uses the Jacobian conjecture as a template to propose a 'Neural Jacobian Conjecture' for one-hidden-layer sigmoid networks, asking whether a positive Jacobian determinant forces global injectivity. Reports complete proofs for the case N = n+1, obtained by invoking GPT-5.5-pro and DeepSeek-V4-pro, and a geometric-topological argument developed with ChatGPT's web interface; the general case N >= n+2 is open. This is a neural analogue, not the polynomial statement.

events.remains: The polynomial statement in full (different question); the general neural case N >= n+2.
events.direction: Supports the neural analogue in the N = n+1 case; no bearing on the polynomial statement.

events.what_happened: Susumu Oda, arXiv:1203.1691, first posted 8 March 2012 (a search snippet gives the early title 'A Short Proof of The Jacobian Conjecture'; the current title is 'On Open Embeddings of Affine Spaces in Affine Varieties and the Jacobian Conjecture'). Versions 1-6 (2012 to Jan 2013) claimed a proof; versions 7-13 were withdrawn (June 2013 to December 2015); version 14 (May 2022) onward uses a different argument; latest is v39 (26 Sep 2026). The current abstract gives the final goal as the Jacobian conjecture in dimension two, calls it a 'faded problem', proves that a normal k-affine surface containing an open subvariety isomorphic to the affine plane equals that subvariety, and states a generalised conjecture GJC_2; it says the results carry over to k via the Lefschetz principle. The comment field (the author's own) says the author revised the draft 'because AI (anthoropic) constructed the counterexample to the Jacobian conjecture'.

events.doubts: Scope has changed across versions: the early titles and claims targeted the full conjecture; the current abstract targets only the plane case. Versions 7-13 were withdrawn, and the argument was replaced in 2022. The abstract still calls the plane case a goal, not a result. The comment's remark about AI concerns the 2026 counterexample and is the author's own, not evidence about the argument. These are signals, not an identified error.

The page lists a later version to v10 (19 Aug 2006) and says 'This paper is withdrawn. Please see the complete paper in math.RA/0512268', with no withdrawal date.

events.remains: n = 2 (as claimed), and n >= 3 by scope.
events.doubts: The page records gaps raised by T. T. Mok about Lemma 3.10, which the author says are addressed in v8. The paper is then marked withdrawn, pointing to another paper.

events.what_happened: Ludwig Kraus, a paper of 1884 which, per Rodríguez Díaz (arXiv:2512.23614; Comptes Rendus Mathématique 364 (2026) 363-370), has as its main result the statement now called the plane Jacobian conjecture. Kraus's final step is flawed; the error concerns controlling ramification at infinity. Wikipedia's infobox credits Kraus with the 1884 formulation (per a search snippet). The journal of the 1884 paper was not identified.
events.delivers: A claimed proof of the planar case, with a flawed final step (per Rodríguez Díaz).
events.remains: n = 2 in full, and n >= 3 by scope.

checked_by.qualification: Author of the 2026 Comptes Rendus analysis; the paper is refereed
checked_by.what_they_did: Located the 1884 paper through zbMATH and identified the final step as flawed, locating the error in controlling ramification at infinity

events.doubts: Per Rodríguez Díaz, the author does not fully repair the proof; some steps 'require further justification or do not go through as stated without modification' (from the arXiv abstract read via a search summary).
events.direction: A claimed planar proof (cuts for the conjecture in dimension two); flawed per the modern analysis.

events.what_happened: Pinchuk, 'A counterexample to the strong real Jacobian conjecture', Math. Z. 217 (1994), 1-4 (per a search result; the Springer page was not opened). Constructs a polynomial map of the real plane whose Jacobian never vanishes but which is not injective (per the search summary; one component's level curves have more than one branch). Sources give 1993 or 1994 for the discovery; the journal year 1994 is recorded. Nguyen's introduction (search snippet) says the real case was 'solved negatively by Pinchuk in 1994'. Peretz (1996, per a search summary) argues that the complex case admits no counterexample of Pinchuk's type.
events.delivers: Refutes the strong real Jacobian conjecture, in which the Jacobian is nonvanishing but not required to be constant. Restricted to the real plane. The sources read do not say whether Pinchuk's Jacobian is constant, so they do not establish that the constant-Jacobian statement over R fails.
events.remains: Whether the constant-Jacobian statement over R fails in dimension 2 is not settled by the sources read. The complex plane case remains open (see alpoge-2026-07-19 for the scope of the 2026 result).
events.direction: Against a strong real version of the conjecture (nonvanishing rather than constant Jacobian). Whether it cuts against the constant-Jacobian statement over R is not established by the sources read.
events.object: A polynomial map R^2 to R^2 with a nowhere-vanishing Jacobian that is not injective (per the search summary; the explicit formula was not read).
people: Pinchuk (initial not given in the sources read)

disputes.summary: Role of Claude Fable 5 in the 2026 counterexample. The AFP entry and Wikipedia credit the model with work leading to the map. The Breakthrough Tracker says Fable reportedly found the example and humans posed the question and checked the algebra. Wikipedia says the method has not been revealed. A Tao comment (reader's comment, not Tao's text) says the result is 'credited to Levent Alpöge, with Claude Fable 5 (Anthropic), not vice versa'. Secondary reports say Akhil Mathew posed the question, and the announcement's own wording was not read.

Announcement date of the counterexample: 19 July 2026 in Wikipedia's lead, the Gao abstract, Gallagher's preprint and the Breakthrough Tracker; 20 July in Wikipedia's citation of the tweet, the AFP entry and Gallagher's reference list. Secondary reports say the tweet was posted on the night of the World Cup final (19 July). The record uses 19 July as the first public written argument.

AI credit for the family in Gallagher's preprint (OpenAI's GPT-5.6-sol) appears only in the Zenodo record page as read through a fetch summary; a search for that model name in connection with the result returned nothing. The PDF could not be extracted to confirm it.
Long's Poisson and Dixmier paper: MathWorld says ChatGPT supplied the construction with AI auditing; the arXiv abstract, comments and page contain no AI statement.

Origin of the conjecture: Kraus (1884) versus Keller (1939). Rodríguez Díaz argues the statement is the main result of Kraus's 1884 paper, whose final step is flawed. The conventional attribution (and the Wikipedia lead, per the fetch) is Keller 1939; a Wikipedia infobox credits Kraus (search snippet). This concerns authorship of the conjecture, not priority of a result.

Pinchuk (1994) is described as refuting 'the real Jacobian conjecture' (Nguyen's introduction, via a search snippet) but as a counterexample to the 'strong real Jacobian conjecture' in the Math. Z. title, whose Jacobian is nonvanishing rather than constant. Whether the real constant-Jacobian statement is refuted is not settled by the sources read.

summary: Found: a dimension-3 counterexample announced in July 2026 and a cluster of follow-ups. Alpöge's map (explicit, degree 7, Jacobian determinant -2, three points in one fibre) refutes the statement for n = 3. Support comes from Tao's digest, an Isabelle/HOL entry in the Archive of Formal Proofs, and my hand check of the three collisions and of the determinant at the origin (not the full constancy). Gallagher's Zenodo preprint (20 July) gives an infinite family in dimension 3, and Gao (31 July) gives counterexamples in every dimension above two, so the failure is not isolated; van den Essen (15 Sep) gives an elementary route to the same example. The plane case n = 2 is open in every source read, including the Wikipedia lead, Meng and Yang, Nguyen and the Oda abstract. No 2026 result is peer reviewed in the sources read; the latest such statement is MathWorld's update of 2 Oct 2026, which gives no verification or review for the counterexample. AI involvement: the announcer's own post, which I could not read directly (X returned HTTP 402), is reported to credit Claude Fable 5 and to thank Fable 'for working overtime'. The AFP entry and Wikipedia repeat the credit; the Breakthrough Tracker says the model found the example and humans posed the question; Wikipedia says the method has not been revealed. This rests on secondary quotations. Gallagher's record, as read through a fetch summary, states that OpenAI's GPT-5.6-sol gave 'substantial mathematical and computational assistance' to the construction of the family. Tao's digest says 'using the Fable AI' and discloses a ChatGPT chatbot used to confirm calculations (checking only). The AFP entry says AI was used for proof engineering without naming a system. van den Essen's abstract credits Alpöge; a search snippet says his PDF mentions Claude Fable 5, but the PDF could not be extracted, so that is unresolved. Moonshine (9 June 2026) credits GPT-5.5-pro and DeepSeek-V4-pro with proofs for a neural analogue, which is a different question. Older literature: claimed proofs by Varshavsky (1999), Kuo, Parusiński and Paunescu (2005), Su (2005-06), Han (2017) and Sazonov (2022-23) were all withdrawn by their authors; Oda's arXiv claim has been revised through 26 Sep 2026 and now targets only the plane case; Preprints.org 202403.0664 (March 2024, not opened) claims a proof over C^n, which the dimension-3 counterexample contradicts. Close calls: (a) The statement is universal over n and over characteristic-0 fields. The n = 3 counterexample refutes it as worded, while n = 2 stays open; whether the judging pass counts this as settling the problem is its call. Pinchuk's 1994 real example is a strong real version with nonvanishing (not constant) Jacobian, so it does not settle the real constant-Jacobian case in these sources. (b) The AI role rests on the announcer's post as reported by others, and the method is undisclosed. (c) Long's Poisson and Dixmier paper: MathWorld says ChatGPT supplied the construction; the arXiv page says nothing. (d) The announcement date is 19 or 20 July; I used 19 July, which Gallagher, Gao and Wikipedia's lead give.
competing_reading: The counterexample is one instance in dimension 3, and Wikipedia's lead calls the plane case the only unresolved one. On that reading the event is a counterexample to a dimension-restricted claim that leaves the plane case open, and the problem is not closed. The opposing reading treats the statement as a single universal claim over every n and every characteristic-0 field, which one counterexample falsifies; the Wikipedia article and Tao's digest frame it that way. On AI: a reading that makes the model's role only search (Tao's and John Cook's accounts treat it as a tool; van den Essen gives an elementary route, which suggests a human could find the map) would count the credit as not load-bearing. The announcer's credit, which I could not read directly, is the strongest reading and makes the model load-bearing.
what_would_settle_it: The announcer's own post text and timestamp, and any PDF he posts (X returned HTTP 402; the Wikipedia article cites a 9 September 2026 post, not read). The full text of van den Essen's arXiv:2609.17795, for its method and any AI sentence. The PDF of Gallagher's Zenodo record, for the exact AI sentence and formulas. Speyer's note, which I could not find. The Pinchuk paper, to see whether its Jacobian is constant, which decides the real constant-Jacobian question. Any journal acceptance or refereeing report for the 2026 counterexample. Sorry-free checks of any Lean repositories the secondary sources mention. The Preprints.org 202403.0664 argument, to locate its error against the explicit map.

incomplete: (1) The announcement itself (Alpöge's X post, 19/20 July 2026) and his 9 Sept 2026 post could not be read; the AI credit and the 'Akhil Mathew' credit rest on secondary quotations, and WebFetch summaries of pages are not raw text, so quoted wording should be checked against the originals. (2) Gallagher's and van den Essen's PDFs could not be extracted; the AI statements for both are from the Zenodo record page (for Gallagher) and an unverified search snippet (for van den Essen). (3) For arXiv items recorded from abstract pages only (Gao, Shaska, Meng-Yang, Wang-Yan, Prellberg, Borisov-Gabber-Vasiu, van den Essen, Long), ai.none_found reflects the abstract and landing page, not the full text; the full papers were not read. (4) Speyer's note, Pinchuk's paper (only a search summary), the Preprints.org claim (403), and the Lean/Isabelle repositories other than the AFP entry were not opened. (5) The Oda, Kuo-Parusiński-Paunescu and Su entries rely on arXiv abstracts; the mathematics was not checked. (6) Several dates are from search summaries (Tian-Sun received/accepted dates from the journal page; Nguyen's journal version from a snippet). (7) The Jacobian determinant was checked by hand only at the origin and the three collisions were checked by hand; constancy of the determinant was not checked by computer. (8) Breakthrough Tracker, lenz.io, KuCoin, The Conversation and minimaxir were used for secondary facts only. (9) No record of the 2026 Lean repositories or the openconjectures thread status; the latest status found is MathWorld's update of 2 Oct 2026.
